reading.body:
Stack Infrastructure's POR03 campus in Hillsboro, Oregon occupies 182,000 square feet of technical space, but the operator has not published a megawatt figure, making it impossible to estimate compute capacity or rank it against other facilities.

Oregon has 133 mapped data centers, only six of which have disclosed power capacity, totaling 182 MW. POR03 would rank seventh by size if a megawatt number existed, but remains unranked without it. The state's disclosure rate is low enough that a large facility can remain invisible to infrastructure accounting simply by withholding one metric.

Technical square footage alone cannot predict IT load or rack density. The same 182,000 square feet could house low-density colocation or high-density GPU clusters depending on power delivery, cooling design, and floor loading, none of which Stack Infrastructure has published. For AI scaling, where power and thermal density drive compute placement, a building size without a power figure is descriptive but not predictive. The campus remains off the compute-capacity map until critical power is disclosed.
